merger_description:
Various corporate credit and asset-backed finance-focused funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Capital Management, L.P. (**Apollo Capital or the Apollo Capital Funds**) propose to indirectly acquire the majority of the equity of UIC Parent Corporation, its subsidiary Curia Global, Inc. and/or the subsidiaries of Curia Global (together, **Curia**) (the Acquisition).

Apollo Capital is a wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of Apollo Global Management, Inc. (**AGM**, together with the indirect subsidiaries of AGM managing the investment funds, **Apollo**). Apollo is a global alternative asset manager organised under the laws of the United States of America and headquartered in New York. As of 31 March 2026, Apollo had approximately US$1.03 trillion of assets under management. Examples of current investments include, inter alia, companies in education, insurance, financial services, and leisure businesses.

Curia is a US-headquartered global contract research, development and manufacturing organisation. Curia has a range of solutions across the drug development spectrum, including in small molecule, generic active pharmaceutical ingredients, biologics, sterile drug product and analytical testing services.

determination_table_content.details:
Apollo Capital Management, L.P. (Apollo Capital) applied for a
notification waiver in respect of the proposal by various corporate
credit and asset-backed finance-focused funds managed by
affiliates of Apollo Capital to indirectly acquire the majority of the
equity of UIC Parent Corporation, its subsidiary Curia Global, Inc.
and/or the subsidiaries of Curia Global (together, Curia), as
described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

Apollo Capital is a wholly owned indirect subsidiary of Apollo Global
Management, Inc. (together with its indirect subsidiaries managing
the investment funds, Apollo). Apollo is a global alternative asset
manager organised under the laws of the United States of America
and headquartered in New York. As of 31 March 2026, Apollo had
approximately US$1.03 trillion of assets under management.
Examples of current investments include, inter alia, companies in
education, insurance, financial services, and leisure businesses.
The target, Curia, is a US-headquartered global contract research,
development and manufacturing organisation. Curia has a range of
solutions across the drug development spectrum, including in small
molecule, generic active pharmaceutical ingredients, biologics,
sterile drug product and analytical testing services.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Apollo and Curia
(including their connected entities) in the supply of contract
research, development and manufacturing solutions across
the drug development spectrum in Australia
b. there are no vertical relationships between the products and
services supplied by the parties in Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
